packageRules.description: Go version: group all Go version updates together to keep them in sync (go.mod, the Go version the workflows and the Containerfile take from go.mod)
Bundle golang.org/x/* updates with Go version bumps so govulncheck sees a consistent set (e.g. golang.org/x/net fixes shipped alongside Go releases)
Go version: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
Go version: require manual review for major updates
Go modules: enable updates for indirect dependencies so transitive security patches (e.g. golang.org/x/net via govulncheck) land without waiting for a direct require to bump
Go modules: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
Go modules: require manual review for major updates on direct requires

Go modules: never open major PRs for indirect deps. Module-path bumps (/v2 -> /v3) cannot be auto-applied without a direct importer, so go mod tidy resets the indirect line to the MVS minimum; major updates land via the parent direct dependency.
Docker images (the release base image and the integration and dev-profile images in tools/versions.env): automerge minor, patch and digest updates
Docker images: require manual review for major updates

Dockerfile and Containerfile: the release image takes its base image and its toolchains from tools/versions.env, go.mod and web/.nvmrc (build arguments), so the Containerfile has no literal image to update; the dockerfile manager finds nothing in it.
GitHub Actions: automerge minor and patch updates
GitHub Actions: automerge major updates after CI passes
Helm charts: automerge minor and patch updates
Helm charts: require manual review for major updates
Makefile-pinned and tools/versions.env tools (custom regex manager): automerge minor and patch updates
Makefile-pinned and tools/versions.env tools (custom regex manager): require manual review for major updates
k6: the image and the version pin move together (deploy/dev/e2e.sh refuses a K6_IMAGE whose tag differs from K6_VERSION), so one pull request carries both

npm client matrix (test/e2e/clients/package.json, R-NPM-045): the eight gate rows are npm aliases that move within their major, in one pull request, because the e2e matrix runs all of them. A new major is a change of the gate rows themselves, decided by the rule of R-NPM-045 and made by hand, so Renovate does not open it. No automerge: the matrix is reviewed.
npm client matrix: no major pull requests (see above)
Node.js: web/.nvmrc and the clients image (E2E_CLIENTS_NODE_IMAGE in tools/versions.env, whose tag starts with the .nvmrc version; make versions-check compares them) move together
Use 'fix' instead of 'chore' for dependency updates (valkey-operator's policy, kept: every automerged dependency PR is a patch release under the conventional commits rule of .releaserc.json)
GitHub Actions: use 'chore' instead of 'fix' for updates

Root release tooling (semantic-release and its presets, package.json): one pull request for the set, because the preset and the writer it renders with must move together; the release-tooling job verifies the set. No automerge: the release path is reviewed by hand.
Angular: every @angular package moves together (web/package.json and its lockfile); the UI is reviewed before a major or a minor moves

customManagers.description: Tool and chart pins of tools/versions.env, each read through the # renovate: comment directly above its line (datasource, depName and an optional registryUrl). The optional registryUrl group keeps Helm chart repositories out of the default registry.
Images pinned by digest in tools/versions.env (the release base image, the Valkey, PostgreSQL, PgBouncer, SeaweedFS, OpenSSL and dev-profile images): tag and digest update together
Update Go version in go.mod (the toolchain of the build, the Containerfile's GO_VERSION build argument, and the workflows' go-version-file)
